problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{2z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$
worked_solution:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{2z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} & =1 \\ 2z & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ z & =\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=1$ is the paraboloid $z=\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}).$
